title: Peach and Prosciutto Salad
subtitle: Ripe summer peaches with prosciutto, rocket and a honey-balsamic dressing
excerpt: Ripe peaches sliced over rocket with prosciutto, torn fresh mozzarella and a honey balsamic dressing. The Italian combination of sweet fruit and cured ham at its simplest and best.
sourceNotes: The pairing of sweet summer fruit with cured ham is a fixture of Italian antipasto, found in dishes such as melone e prosciutto (melon with Parma ham) and the Emilian tradition of matching prosciutto crudo with fresh fruit. The peach version is a British and American adaptation of this tradition that became popular in the 1990s and 2000s as good prosciutto became widely available.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble within 30 minutes of serving. Peaches discolour and the prosciutto dries out if left longer.

content.text: Peach and prosciutto is a summer dish that depends entirely on ingredient quality. The peaches must be ripe enough to give slightly when pressed and smell sweet at the stalk end; firm, flavourless supermarket peaches produce a disappointing result. The prosciutto should be sliced thin, ideally from the deli counter. Everything else is a matter of assembly.

items.prepNote: ripe, halved and stoned, sliced into wedges

content.text: Whisk together {{balsamic-vinegar}} of balsamic vinegar, {{olive-oil}} of olive oil, {{honey}} of honey, {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt and {{black-pepper}} of pepper. Arrange the rocket on a large plate or platter. Lay the prosciutto slices over the rocket, loosely folded. Add the peach wedges and torn mozzarella if using. Scatter the basil over. Drizzle with the dressing and serve immediately.

items.fix: This salad is only worth making in summer, ideally with peaches from a farmers' market or farm shop that have been allowed to ripen fully. If in doubt, use nectarines, which tend to be sweeter even when slightly underripe.

items.cause: Sliced too thick, or dried out from being left uncovered.
items.fix: Prosciutto should be sliced paper-thin. Keep it covered with clingfilm until the moment of serving.

content.text: Prosciutto with sweet fruit is a classic Italian antipasto. The Italian original uses melon rather than peach, but the idea is the same: the sweetness of the fruit against the salt of the ham. The peach version is a British summer adaptation that now appears regularly at warm-weather lunches and garden dinners.
